questions.question_text: The resting membrane potential exists because:
options: Ion concentrations differ inside and outside the cell
questions.correct_answer: Ion concentrations differ inside and outside the cell
questions.explanation: Uneven Na⁺ and K⁺ distribution creates potential difference.

questions.question_text: An action potential begins when:
options: Threshold is reached and voltage-gated channels open
Only K⁺ channels open first always
questions.correct_answer: Threshold is reached and voltage-gated channels open
questions.explanation: Threshold triggers rapid depolarisation.

questions.question_text: During depolarisation, which ions primarily enter the neuron?
questions.explanation: Na⁺ influx drives the rising phase of the action potential.

questions.question_text: Repolarisation involves:
questions.explanation: K⁺ efflux restores negative internal charge.

questions.question_text: The refractory period limits how frequently a neuron can fire.
questions.explanation: Channels must reset before another action potential.

questions.question_text: A sub-threshold stimulus:
options: Does not produce a full action potential
questions.correct_answer: Does not produce a full action potential
questions.explanation: All-or-nothing response requires reaching threshold.

questions.question_text: Action potentials propagate along the:
questions.explanation: Axons carry impulses away from the cell body.

questions.question_text: Nerve impulses are electrical signals caused by ion movement across membranes.
questions.explanation: Voltage changes arise from controlled ion channel activity.

questions.question_text: Name the period when the neuron cannot fire another impulse immediately.
questions.explanation: Refractory period follows each action potential.

questions.question_text: Which ion's channels open first during the rising phase of an action potential?
questions.explanation: Voltage-gated Na⁺ channels open to depolarise the membrane.

question_bank.title: Fluid Pressure and Flow — Biology Assessment

questions.question_text: Blood pressure is highest in:
questions.explanation: Arteries receive blood directly from ventricular contraction.

questions.question_text: Narrower vessels for the same flow rate have:
questions.explanation: Continuity: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂, so smaller area means higher speed.

questions.question_text: Pressure in a fluid increases with:
questions.explanation: Hydrostatic pressure grows with depth (P = hρg).

questions.question_text: The circulatory system analogy uses fluid flow to explain:
options: How vessel diameter affects flow speed
questions.correct_answer: How vessel diameter affects flow speed
questions.explanation: Pipe diameter models blood vessel resistance to flow.

questions.question_text: Atherosclerosis narrows vessels and can raise blood pressure.
questions.explanation: Narrowed lumens increase resistance and pressure.

questions.question_text: In the Flow screen, reducing pipe diameter:
options: Increases flow speed in that section
questions.correct_answer: Increases flow speed in that section
questions.explanation: Same volume flow through smaller area means higher velocity.

questions.question_text: Denser fluids at the same depth exert:
questions.explanation: P = hρg depends on density ρ.

questions.question_text: Fluid pressure acts equally in all directions at a given depth.
questions.explanation: Fluids transmit pressure uniformly at a level.

questions.question_text: Name the principle stating flow rate is constant in a closed pipe system.
questions.explanation: Continuity equation links area and velocity.

questions.question_text: What biological system is modelled by fluid pressure and flow in this sim?
questions.explanation: Blood circulation parallels fluid flow in pipes.
